gate_results.notes: VAL-001 is about a PRODUCED PLAYER, not about unit tests, and this record does not conflate them. The command was invoked headlessly on a clean checkout at 253c545bee60d925d4291d19692c90e571a9d506: Unity 6000.1.8f1 -batchmode -quit -nographics -executeMethod NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Editor.WindowsStandaloneBuildCommand.Build with -nsc-output pointing OUTSIDE the repository. Unity exit code 0. MEASURED at the reported output path C:/nscrev/builds/nsc113-20260925: NoSafeCircle.exe exists and is NON-EMPTY at 667,648 bytes, sha256 c52a78dcbe24e853 (full hash in the verification artifact); its accompanying NoSafeCircle_Data directory exists with 14 entries; the standard player layout MonoBleedingEdge, D3D12 and NoSafeCircle_BurstDebugInformation_DoNotShip is present; total build size 138,387,335 bytes. The working tree was 0 dirty before and after, so the build did not mutate the repository - which required passing -nsc-output explicitly, because the command's DefaultOutputDirectory is Build/Windows, INSIDE the tree, and the default would have dirtied it. The 6 passing WindowsStandaloneBuildCommandTests are recorded as supporting evidence only: they exercise argument handling and scene resolution, NOT a produced player, and on their own they do not satisfy this gate. LOG NORMALIZATION, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: record_delivery refused the raw build log because it carried trailing whitespace on 12 of its 6,032 lines, with the message that the authoritative Unity runner must normalize logs before packaging. run_unity_tests_clean.ps1 does exactly that, but it runs TESTS and does not perform player builds, so no authoritative runner exists for a build log. I stripped trailing whitespace myself - 12 lines, no other change - and packaged that file. I did NOT relabel the artifact type to evade the check. The unmodified original remains at the scratchpad path recorded in the build verification artifact.
